stem: A client has used clobetasol, a super-high-potency topical corticosteroid, for a prolonged period and now has visibly thin skin with telangiectasia and striae. Which adverse effect is most consistent with these findings?

options.B: Dependent edema as the characteristic local toxicity of clobetasol.
options.C: Lichenification from increased dermal collagen production.
options.D: Local corticosteroid skin atrophy with striae and telangiectasia.

rationale: The current clobetasol propionate label identifies the product as a super-high-potency topical corticosteroid and states that local adverse reactions are more likely with prolonged use or higher-potency corticosteroids. Listed local reactions include skin atrophy, striae, and telangiectasias. Therefore D is correct. The other findings are not the characteristic local toxicity pattern described in the label.
educational_objective: Recognize skin atrophy, striae, and telangiectasia as local toxicity from prolonged use of a high-potency topical corticosteroid such as clobetasol.
source_organization: DailyMed / U.S. Food and Drug Administration labeling
source_version_date: DailyMed label updated April 23, 2026; prescribing information revised April 2026
source_locator: Warnings and Precautions §5.2 Local Adverse Reactions with Topical Corticosteroids: reactions more likely with prolonged use/higher potency and include atrophy, striae, telangiectasias. Adverse Reactions §6.1 also lists skin atrophy and telangiectasia.
source_claim_supported: Prolonged use of super-high-potency clobetasol can produce local skin atrophy, striae, and telangiectasia.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: recognize local/systemic medication adverse effects, monitor response, and provide safe medication teaching.
blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — topical corticosteroid local toxicity

source_original.stem: A client has used a high-potency topical corticosteroid for a prolonged period and now has visibly thin skin with telangiectasia and striae. Which adverse effect is most consistent with these findings?

options.A: Hyperkeratosis with progressive skin thickening is the characteristic local toxicity of prolonged clobetasol use.
options.B: Dependent edema is the expected local adverse effect that produces striae and visible superficial vessels.
options.C: Lichenification is the typical corticosteroid-induced change caused by increased dermal collagen production.
options.D: Skin atrophy with striae and telangiectasia is consistent with local toxicity from prolonged use of a high-potency topical corticosteroid.

source_original.rationale: FDA labeling for high-potency topical corticosteroids such as clobetasol lists local adverse reactions including skin atrophy, striae, and telangiectasia, especially with prolonged or higher-potency use. These findings therefore represent local corticosteroid toxicity rather than a therapeutic effect.
source_original.source_detail: Warnings/Adverse Reactions — local corticosteroid reactions including atrophy, striae, and telangiectasia. Revised 04/2026, version 100, effective 2026-04-23; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: medication administration, adverse effects/interactions, monitoring, reconciliation and teaching. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained the local corticosteroid-toxicity construct and key D, specified clobetasol/super-high potency to directly match the current label, simplified distractors into parallel dermatologic findings, and reduced difficulty from hard to medium because the final item tests a direct labeled toxicity pattern.

audit_findings.source_authority: Current DailyMed/FDA clobetasol label; NCSBN 2026 blueprint
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item uses the exact labeled local toxicity findings and does not imply that all patients using clobetasol will develop them.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect; corticosteroid toxicity is associated with atrophy rather than hyperkeratotic thickening.
distractor_audit.B: Incorrect; dependent edema is not the characteristic local reaction explaining striae/telangiectasia.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect; lichenification is not the labeled corticosteroid-induced pattern and the mechanism is misstated.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only D matches the entire triad of thin skin/atrophy, striae, and telangiectasia after prolonged high-potency topical steroid use.
audit_findings.cueing: All alternatives are local dermatologic interpretations and are parallel in scope.
audit_findings.blueprint: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — adverse-effect recognition and safe topical medication use.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked the April 2026 clobetasol label, §5.2/§6.1, all alternatives, rationale, objective, difficulty, ambiguity, cueing and NCSBN mapping. D remained uniquely correct.
